suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` reads a property without a null check. When evt.destinationCalendar is null or [] (handleNewBooking sets null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. WHY: Booking a Google Meet event with no destination calendar throws a TypeError and the booking fails. Before, `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` fell back to Cal Video. HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: For video results, `credentialId` is now `undefined` instead of `result.credentialId`. createMeeting does return credentialId (videoClient.ts:78). WHY: Video booking references are saved without a credentialId. handleCancelBooking (L491) only calls deleteMeeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so Zoom/Daily meetings are no longer deleted on cancel, and other credential-scoped lookups also break. HOW: `credentialId: result.credentialId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: updateLocation now takes externalCalendarId and credentialId only from the result. CalendarManager.updateEvent returns neither field (CalendarManager.ts L313-322), and the old fallback to evt.destinationCalendar was removed. WHY: After a location edit, the new calendar references are saved with externalCalendarId and credentialId undefined. Later updates and cancellations then fall back to the legacy path that iterates all credentials, or target the wrong or primary calendar. HOW: return externalCalendarId and credentialId from updateEvent, or keep the destination-calendar fallback.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fallback branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, so it always returns undefined. The same pattern appears in deleteEvent at L315-317. WHY: The previous fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost. Update and delete for references without externalCalendarId now get calendarId undefined and fail or hit the wrong calendar. HOW: fall back to the destination matching this credential, e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === this.credential.id)?.externalId`, or to the first entry.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: destinationCalendar becomes `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. WHY: For COLLECTIVE events where the first host has no destination calendar, every other host's destination calendar is silently dropped. That is exactly the multi-host case this PR is meant to fix. HOW: initialize with `[]` and push the team calendars into it, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: createEvent always uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, even though EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination/credential, including other hosts' credentials. WHY: For collective events, a second host's Office365 credential posts to `/me/calendars/<main host's calendar id>/events`, which fails (404) or lands in the wrong calendar, so that host is never invited. Lark (L128) and the CalDAV BaseCalendarService (L156) have the same problem. HOW: select the destination whose credentialId matches this service's credential, using the new credentialId argument the way Google does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The recurring-series delete block, which iterates all of the organizer's calendar credentials × all updatedBookings, now sits inside the per-reference loop. WHY: With N calendar references (multiple collective hosts), the whole series is deleted N times with the organizer's credentials, causing redundant API calls and 404/410 errors. The other hosts' recurring events are still not deleted, because only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` is used. HOW: run the recurring-series delete once, outside the loop, and use each reference's own credential for its events.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The condition was inverted: before, `slug` was set when billing was NOT enabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }`), and now it is set only when billing IS enabled. WHY: Self-hosted instances without billing create organizations with no slug. With billing enabled, the slug is set immediately and skips the requestedSlug/payment flow. HOW: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The refactored loadUsers no longer selects `organization { slug }` for dynamic users, but users are later typed as IsFixedAwareUser, which requires `organization: { slug: string }` (L355). The rewrite also turns all non-Prisma errors (including an empty dynamic user list) into a generic 500. WHY: Downstream code that reads `user.organization.slug` for dynamic group bookings gets undefined, and bad requests surface as 500 instead of 4xx. HOW: restore the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` select.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar now crash instead of falling back to Cal Video.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `evt.destinationCalendar` is now an array, and it can be null or empty. handleNewBooking sets it to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar; other handlers use `[]`. In both cases `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError whenever the location is Google Meet. That is exactly the case the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` check handled by falling back to Cal Video. Use optional chaining: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new loadUsers catch copies raw Prisma error messages into a client-facing HttpError, which can skip the central Prisma redaction.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new catch block turns a `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` into `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`. Normally `getServerErrorFromUnknown` (`packages/lib/server/getServerErrorFromUnknown.ts:45-46,78-80`) redacts Prisma errors before they are sent. Since this error is already an `HttpError`, it takes the HttpError branch instead (line 54), so the unredacted text can reach the booking API caller. That text can include the query invocation, model and field names, constraint details and server file paths. Fix: rethrow the Prisma error unchanged so the central handler redacts it, or use a generic message.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws TypeError when the destinationCalendar array is null or empty and the location is Google Meet.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` can be empty: handleNewBooking now passes null when there is no event-type or organizer calendar, and other callers pass []. In that case `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined, so `.integration` throws whenever location is Google Meet. Booking creation crashes instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The updateEvent fallback compares against the falsy externalCalendarId, so calendarId is always undefined and the Google update fails.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`. That never finds a real calendar, so selectedCalendar is undefined. `calendar.events.update` is called without a calendarId and rejects. Before this change it used the destination calendar's externalId. Fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId or to 'primary'. deleteEvent at lines 315-317 has the same dead lookup.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: For collective events, team member destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar.
suggestions.suggestionContent: destinationCalendar becomes null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so the collected team member calendars are lost and no events are created in their calendars. Default to [] instead of null.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When destinationCalendar is null or [], the first element `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError for any Google Meet booking where the organizer has no destination calendar. Many callers now pass [] in this case. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`. That is a lookup against an empty or undefined key, so it effectively always returns undefined. The old code fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Now updateEvent sends `calendarId: undefined` to Google, and deleteEvent (line 315-317) quietly falls back to "primary", which may be the wrong calendar. Fall back to the main host destination calendar's externalId (or match by credential) instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, destinationCalendar is set to null. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, so the destination calendars of every other COLLECTIVE host are silently dropped. Initialize it to [] instead of null so team calendars are still appended.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Reading `.integration` on the first entry of a possibly-empty destinationCalendar array crashes Meet bookings when the user has no destination calendar.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The producers now pass `[]` or `null` when the user has no destination calendar, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError for Google Meet bookings. The old code used optional chaining. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Office365 createEvent always targets the first (organizer's) destination calendar, even when EventManager calls it with a collective team member's credential.
suggestions.suggestionContent: For collective team events, `EventManager` now creates one event per member destination calendar, each with that member's credential, and passes `credentialId` to `createEvent`. Office365 ignores `credentialId` and builds the URL from `destinationCalendar[0]`, the organizer's calendar. With the team member's token, the request goes to a calendar that belongs to someone else, so the event fails or lands in the wrong calendar. Accept `credentialId` and select `event.destinationCalendar?.find(c => c.credentialId === credentialId)`, as the Google service does. The same fix is needed in the Lark service.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The condition for setting the organization slug is inverted: it is now set when billing is enabled instead of when it is disabled.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The original `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` set the slug directly only when team billing was DISABLED. When billing was enabled, the slug went into `metadata.requestedSlug` and was only applied after payment. The rewrite drops the `!`, so it sets `slug` when billing is enabled and omits it when billing is disabled. Orgs on self-hosted or non-billing setups are now created with no slug, and billing setups get the slug before payment. Restore the negation: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The fallback lookup in Google updateEvent and deleteEvent can never match, so it always yields undefined.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. a calendar whose externalId is null or undefined, so it never finds one and returns undefined. The old fallback used `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Now updates send `calendarId: undefined`, and deletes (line 315-317) always fall back to "primary", even when the event lives in the host's selected destination calendar. Fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId (or match by credential id) instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is read without optional chaining and throws when there is no destination calendar.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` is undefined when `destinationCalendar` is null or empty, which handleNewBooking and the other handlers in this diff do produce. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. The new `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError for a Google Meet booking with no destination calendar, which is exactly the case the Cal Video fallback was meant to handle. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Team members' destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar, because `evt.destinationCalendar` is null.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `destinationCalendar` falls back to `null` (not `[]`) when neither the event type nor the organizer has one. Then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` short-circuits, and the collective members' calendars collected at lines 990-994 are thrown away. Default to `[]`, or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. isTeamAdmin (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264) already matches role ADMIN or OWNER, so the && means only OWNERs pass. WHY: team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN, which contradicts the variable's intent. HOW: use `!!(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId))` alone, or `||` the two checks. Also skip the queries when `booking.eventType?.teamId` is null instead of querying teamId 0.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: EventManager is built with the caller's (`ctx.user`) credentials. updateCalendarAttendees then updates the calendar events referenced by `booking.references`, which belong to the booking organizer. WHY: when an attendee or team admin (both allowed by the permission check) adds guests, the caller has no credential matching the organizer's calendar or video references, so the organizer's calendar event is never updated with the new attendees even though the DB and emails say it was. HOW: build EventManager from the organizer's user and credentials. `booking.user` with `credentials` is already included in the query; pass it through getUsersCredentials or the equivalent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` gets the raw input list, not `uniqueGuests`. WHY: in email-manager, any attendee whose email is in `newGuests` gets an AttendeeScheduledEmail. A submitted guest who was already an attendee is filtered out of the insert but still gets a duplicate 'new booking' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. The catch also swallows the error without logging it. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests` and log `err`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: blacklisted emails are lowercased, but the `guest` value is compared without normalization. The duplicate check against existing attendees is also case-sensitive. WHY: a caller can add a blacklisted address such as `Blocked@Domain.com` and get it emailed by the system, bypassing BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Changing case also lets the same person be added as an attendee twice. HOW: compare `guest.toLowerCase()` against the blacklist and against `attendee.email.toLowerCase()`, and dedupe the input case-insensitively.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `guests` is an unbounded `z.array(z.string().email())` with no max, and the handler lets any booking attendee (match on session email) add arbitrary addresses. It does no check against seatsPerTimeSlot, seatsShowAttendees or booking status. WHY: one request can insert thousands of attendees and make the server send a calendar invite from the organizer to each address, which turns the endpoint into an email-spam relay. On seated events it can exceed capacity and expose every attendee's email to the others. HOW: add `.max(N)` to the array, reject cancelled or past bookings, and enforce the seat limits and seatsShowAttendees rules for seated event types.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `isInvalidEmail` is never reset in onSuccess, when emails are edited, or when the dialog is closed through `onOpenChange` (overlay or Esc). Closing through onOpenChange also does not clear `multiEmailValue`. Separately, `message` in onError is a template string that is always truthy, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback can never run. WHY: after one invalid attempt the error banner stays visible on later valid submissions and on reopening, and stale emails from a dismissed dialog persist. HOW: reset `isInvalidEmail` in onSuccess and in the onOpenChange handler. Build the message conditionally, e.g. `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The `||` fallback to `unable_to_add_guests` never runs because the template-literal message is always truthy.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `message` is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which always contains at least ": ", so it is never falsy. The `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never be used. When `err.data` is undefined (for example on a network or transport error), the toast shows "undefined: <raw message>". Build the message conditionally instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The subject line uses `attendees[0].name`, but the attendee list is unordered and this PR adds attendees with empty names.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`, which assumes the first attendee is the original booker. The list comes from `prisma.booking.update({ include: { attendees: true } })` with no `orderBy` (`addGuests.handler.ts:92-106`), so its order is not guaranteed. The handler also inserts new guests with `name: ""`. If a new guest comes first, the subject reads "Guests Added: X with  at ...". Add `orderBy: { id: 'asc' }` to the include, or pick the first attendee that has a name.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Mixed-case emails bypass the guest blacklist because only the blacklist side is lowercased.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but the guest emails they are checked against are not. A blocked address written with different casing (e.g. `Blocked@Domain.com`) gets past the blacklist, is added as an attendee and receives booking emails. The same exact-match check against existing attendees also lets duplicates in through case differences. Fix: lowercase (and trim) both sides before comparing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The handler passes the raw `guests` input to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so existing attendees in the list get a new booking-confirmation email.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `email-manager.ts` treats its second argument as the list of newly added attendees. Each attendee in that list gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`; everyone else gets `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. The handler passes the unfiltered `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. So if the request includes an email that is already an attendee, that existing attendee gets a booking-confirmation email instead of the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` so the email manager gets the list it expects.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The FORBIDDEN error message is "you_do_not_have_permission", and the client translates it with t(err.message). That key isn't in apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json; grep found no match, while booking_not_found and the other keys used here are present. Users will see the raw key. Add the translation, or use a key that already exists.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `message` is a template string, so it is never empty. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback (a new locale key added in this PR) can never be shown. When err.data is undefined, the toast also shows the literal text "undefined: ...". Build the message conditionally and fall back to the translated key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The tooltip text "Remove email" is hard-coded English. The same component translates its other text with t("add_another"), so this string skips translation. Use t() with a locale key instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`, so it is true only when the user is both admin and owner. The name says either role is enough. Change it to `||`, or rename the variable, so the name and the permission check agree.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Emails are sent using the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests` list.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `uniqueGuests` (the input with existing attendees and blacklisted emails removed) is computed at line 74, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input. sendAddGuestsEmails uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to choose between the 'scheduled' and 'guests added' templates. So an attendee who was already on the booking but appears in the request gets a new booking-confirmation email instead of the update notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` combines the two checks with && instead of ||.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, but the expression requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true. A team admin who is not the owner (or the reverse, depending on what these helpers return) is wrongly refused with FORBIDDEN. Use `||`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are compared as typed, so mixed-case blacklisted emails get through.
suggestions.suggestionContent: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased, but `guest` is compared without lowercasing. 'Bad@x.com' does not match the blacklisted 'bad@x.com'. The same applies to the existing-attendee check. Lowercase `guest` before both comparisons.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The server lets the same guest be added to a booking more than once: duplicates within the input, emails differing only in case, and two requests running at once all get through.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Uniqueness is only enforced on the client. Normalize and dedupe on the server: `const normalized = [...new Set(guests.map(g => g.trim().toLowerCase()))]`. Compare against `attendee.email.toLowerCase()`. Also add a uniqueness `.refine` to ZAddGuestsInputSchema. To block concurrent duplicate inserts, run the read and insert in a `prisma.$transaction` or add a unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and use `skipDuplicates: true`. Finally, pass the deduped `uniqueGuests` to sendAddGuestsEmails, not the raw `guests`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.relevantFile: addGuests handler (file path not specified in analysis)
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The admin/owner permission check uses && where || is intended.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The admin/owner authorization check uses && instead of ||. As written, it may wrongly deny or allow access. The reviewer noted this as outside their assigned scope.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.relevantFile: addGuests handler (file path not specified in analysis)
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Emails are sent to `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler sends emails to `guests` instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests` list. This can send duplicate emails or email guests who are already attendees. The reviewer noted this as outside their assigned scope.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.relevantFile: addGuests handler (file path not specified in analysis)
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The blacklist check is case-sensitive because guest emails are not lowercased.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist check compares guest emails without lowercasing them, so a blacklisted address in different letter case can get past the check. The reviewer noted this as outside their assigned scope.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), and that whole object is saved as credential.key. WHY: the stored key becomes {success:true,data:{...}}, so the next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) in googleAuth (line 75) throws and the Google Calendar credential stops working after its first refresh. HOW: save the parsed payload instead: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when sync is enabled, the helper returns a raw fetch Response, but each caller expects the same shape its own refreshFunction returns. Google reads `res.data.access_token`, Hubspot treats the result as a HubspotToken, and zoho-bigin/zohocrm read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios shape). WHY: with CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, these integrations either throw a TypeError on `undefined.access_token` / `undefined.error` or save a Response object as the credential key. HOW: have the helper return a normalized parsed JSON body, or have each caller handle a Response in the sync branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the third argument (userId) passed to refreshOAuthTokens is `credentialId`, not the credential's userId. WHY: in sync mode the request asks the parent app for tokens of `calcomUserId=<credential id>`, which belongs to an unrelated user. The wrong user's tokens could then be saved on this credential, a cross-account credential mix-up. HOW: pass the credential's userId; store `credential.userId` in the constructor and pass it here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the same literal property name, not a wildcard. Separately, the function always fills a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token". WHY: in sync mode z.object strips every key except access_token, so expiry fields are lost (Zoom computes expiry_date from undefined expires_in → NaN). Office365 calendar's schema has `refresh_token` optional and spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credentials (line 264), so when Microsoft omits refresh_token the real stored token is overwritten with "refresh_token" and every later refresh fails. Zoom also writes newTokens.refresh_token into the key. HOW: use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` (or a catchall) for the minimum schema, and do not invent a refresh_token; leave it undefined so callers keep the existing one.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: appStoreMetadata is indexed with `app.slug`, but the map is keyed by the app directory name (see _appRegistry.ts:17 `appStoreMetadata[app.dirName]`). WHY: apps whose slug differs from their dirName (google-calendar/googlecalendar, office365-calendar/office365calendar, etc.) always get a 404 'App not found', so credential sync cannot work for the main OAuth apps. HOW: also select `dirName` from prisma.app and look up `appStoreMetadata[app.dirName]`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when state.teamId is set, the function checks only that the user is an accepted member, creates the team credential, and returns early. throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam runs only on the non-team path, where teamId is always null, so it does nothing. WHY: any non-admin team member can install or overwrite app credentials (Stripe, Zoom, Salesforce, etc.) on a team by passing `{teamId}` in the OAuth state, bypassing the admin requirement. HOW: call `await throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state.teamId, userId })` inside the team branch before prisma.credential.create.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getClient now does an unconditional refresh-token request and DB update every time the service is constructed. It checks `response.statusText !== "OK"`, and it still builds the jsforce Connection with the old `credentialKey.access_token`. WHY: statusText is empty under HTTP/2/undici, so valid responses are rejected, and because this.conn is the rejected promise every Salesforce operation fails. The refreshed token is also never used. Every instantiation adds an extra network round-trip plus a DB write, and in sync mode refresh_token is overwritten by the parseRefreshTokenResponse placeholder logic. HOW: check `response.ok`, refresh only when expired, and pass `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` / `instance_url` to the Connection.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the webhook secret is compared with `!==` (not constant-time), and the body is parsed with `.parse`, which throws on bad input. WHY: this endpoint can write arbitrary credentials for any userId. A non-constant-time compare leaks timing information about the secret, and malformed bodies or decryption failures (JSON.parse at line 57) produce unhandled 500s instead of 400s. HOW: compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, and use safeParse with a 400 response.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The credential ID is sent as calcomUserId to the credential sync endpoint, so another user's OAuth tokens can be fetched and stored.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The refreshOAuthTokens call passes `credentialId` (the credential's primary key) where it expects the Cal.com user ID. When credential sync is enabled, the parent app is asked for the Zoho Bigin tokens of whichever user happens to have that ID. Those tokens are then saved to this credential. One user's Zoho access tokens can end up on another user's account, and that user's CRM data can be read through them. Pass the credential's userId instead. For example, pass `credential.userId` into refreshAccessToken and forward it here, as the other integrations do.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Webhook secret is compared with `!==` instead of a constant-time comparison, so it leaks timing information.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook secret check compares the request header to CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET with `!==`. That comparison stops at the first byte that differs, so its timing reveals how much of a guess is correct. This endpoint creates or overwrites credentials for any userId, so recovering the secret would let an attacker plant their own OAuth tokens for any user. Compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual instead: check that the header is a string, check that the lengths match, then compare.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The credential id is passed in the userId slot of refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint gets it as calcomUserId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens` documents its third argument as the user that owns the credential and sends it to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId` (`credential.id`). When credential sync is enabled, the parent app gets a credential id labelled as a Cal.com user id, so it returns tokens for the wrong user or none at all. For team credentials the userId check is also skipped incorrectly. Pass the credential's userId instead: thread `credential.userId` into `refreshAccessToken`, as the other adapters do.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse wrapper, but the code still stores its result directly as the credential key.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` returned the credential object. `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns `{ success, data }` instead. `key` is still written straight to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}`. Later reads of `credential.key.access_token`/`refresh_token` will get undefined and Google auth will break. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: An invalid refresh response used to be logged and tolerated; it now throws, and the caller's `tokenResponse.success &&` fallback can never run.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Before this change, `safeParse` failures were logged and the existing credentials were kept, so the refresh was best-effort. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure, so a token response that doesn't match the schema now makes the whole calendar operation fail. The `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` guard on the next line is now dead code, and the diagnostic log was removed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId, but this call passes credentialId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third parameter of `refreshOAuthTokens` is the Cal.com userId that gets sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. This call passes `credentialId`, so the sync endpoint will get tokens for the wrong user, or none. Pass the credential's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod SafeParseReturn (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credential. Before this PR, `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credential object itself. Now `data: { key }` saves `{success: true, data: {...}}` into credential.key. On the next construction, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 throws, so every Google Calendar credential breaks permanently after its first token refresh. Use `.data`: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response`. That object has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. The catch block swallows it and returns the expired auth, so Google tokens are never refreshed in sync mode. Await `res.json()` when the sync path is used, or make the helper return parsed JSON in a consistent shape.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the same string, "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first. The schema ends up as `access_token` plus a nonsense optional key. Because zod's default object mode strips unknown keys, the expiry fields (`expiry_date`, `expires_in`) and any real `refresh_token` are dropped. Line 26 then always replaces the refresh token with the placeholder "refresh_token". Callers save this stripped data, so the stored credentials lose their expiry. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `credentialId` (the credential's primary key) is passed where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the user id. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong `calcomUserId` and can return another user's tokens, which are then saved on this credential. Pass the credential's `userId` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The Google refresh path saves the whole safeParse result (`{success,data}`) as the credential key instead of the parsed token data.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13-30) returns the zod SafeParseReturn object, not the parsed data. Before this change, this code used googleCredentialSchema.parse, which returned the data. Now `key` is `{success:true,data:{...}}`, and it gets written into credential.key. That corrupts every refreshed Google credential: access_token and refresh_token end up nested under `data`. Fix: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;`, or check `.success` first and then use `.data`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Zoho Bigin passes credential.id where refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com userId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) uses its third argument as `calcomUserId` in the sync request and to decide whether to sync at all. Here the argument is `credentialId`, which is credential.id (line 53). The sync endpoint is asked for tokens belonging to whichever user happens to have that id. Pass the credential's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the Google, Zoho and HubSpot callers read `.data` or treat it as a token object.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw `fetch` Response. Several callers changed in this PR assume the old return shape:
- Google reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`.
- zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217 reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`.
- zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 reads `tokenInfo.data.error`.
- hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 treats the result as a HubspotToken.

A Response has no `.data`, so these paths throw (TypeError on undefined) or silently misbehave whenever CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set. Either have refreshOAuthTokens return a value with the same shape callers expect (for example, parsed JSON wrapped in `{data}`), or update each caller to `await response.json()` in the sync case.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The whole safeParse result object is saved as the credential key instead of the parsed data.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParseReturn object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credentials. The diff writes that whole object to `credential.key`, so the stored credential gets wrapped in `{success:true,data:{...}}` and its structure breaks. Use `.data` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The credential id is passed where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the Cal.com user id.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is the user id, which is sent as `calcomUserId`. Here it is `credentialId`, so the sync endpoint is asked for tokens for the wrong user. The function also gets a non-null value even for team credentials, which should skip the sync. Pass the credential's `userId` instead. That means passing it into `refreshAccessToken`, which currently receives only `credentialId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: With credential sync on, the code reads `.data` on a fetch Response, which has no such property.
suggestions.suggestionContent: With credential sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response`, but this code expects the googleapis/axios shape (`res.data`). The token is then undefined and the refresh always fails. Either normalise the sync response inside `refreshOAuthTokens` (for example, `await response.json()` wrapped as `{ data }`), or handle both shapes at each call site.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The admin-access check can only ever run with teamId null, so it never checks anything.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` is called only after the teamId branch has already returned, so it always gets `teamId: null` and checks nothing. Meanwhile any accepted team member, admin or not, can create team credentials. Move the admin check into the teamId branch, before `prisma.credential.create`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The decryption key silently falls back to an empty string instead of failing fast.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` passes an empty string as the AES key when the variable is missing. Today the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED guard prevents this, but a crypto key should never quietly fall back to an empty value. Throw (or return a 500) when the key is missing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `retryCount > 1` branch of the OR in deleteMany has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter and no `scheduled: false` filter. The SMS cron will delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. WHY: retryCount is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder table. As soon as another cron or path starts incrementing it, this SMS-only cleanup will silently wipe reminders of other methods. HOW: Scope the branch: `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every falsy return or exception from twilio.scheduleSMS increments retryCount. That includes the intentional `return;` when the user or team is locked for SMS (twilioProvider.ts:92-95), plus checkSMSRateLimit throws and transient Twilio or network errors. WHY: After 2 cron runs these reminders are permanently deleted by the new deleteMany branch. Before this change they would have been retried until the scheduled date. Reminders for temporarily locked or rate-limited accounts, or ones hit by a short outage, are now silently lost. HOW: Only count failures that are permanent (for example, Twilio invalid-number error codes). Don't increment when sending is locked or rate-limited.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (for example, P2025 because the reminder was deleted concurrently when the booking was cancelled, or a DB connectivity error, which may also be what triggered the original catch), the exception escapes the for loop. WHY: That aborts processing of every remaining unscheduled reminder in this run and makes the cron return a 500. Before this change, one bad reminder could not stop the batch. HOW: Wrap the retry-count update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany({ where: { id }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })` and log any failure.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This cleanup used to delete only SMS reminders. The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, so the SMS cron now deletes WorkflowReminder rows of every method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) once their retryCount passes 1, including rows that are already scheduled. The email and WhatsApp crons could previously count on this job leaving their rows alone. That stops being true as soon as any other path increments `retryCount`. Scope the branch to SMS: `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: An unguarded prisma update inside the catch block can throw, stopping the loop and failing the whole cron run.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The catch block now runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update` with no error handling. This catch also covers failures of the success-path update on lines 169-177. If the reminder row was deleted at the same time (booking cancelled or rescheduled, or an overlapping cron run's deleteMany), the update throws P2025. It can also throw if the DB is having trouble. That exception escapes the for-loop, every remaining reminder in this batch is skipped, and the handler returns 500. Before this change, the catch only logged and the loop continued. Wrap the increment in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany({ where: { id }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })`, which does not throw when the row is missing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: retryCount is incremented from a stale value, so overlapping cron runs lose increments.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` writes a value derived from the findMany snapshot. If two cron invocations overlap and both process the same unscheduled reminder, both write N+1, so a failed attempt goes uncounted and the retry limit is not enforced as intended. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` here and in the catch block.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The retryCount branch of the OR in the cleanup deleteMany has no SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes reminders of any method.
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the cleanup query, `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` only applies to the first OR branch. The `retryCount > 1` branch matches every WorkflowReminder, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP ones. Retry counting in this PR is SMS-only, and this endpoint is meant to clean up SMS reminders only. Move the method filter outside the OR so the two sides agree.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: When the message is empty or sendTo is missing, the reminder is neither scheduled nor counted as a retry, so it is retried forever.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new retry limit misses one failure path. If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is null, nothing is updated, and the reminder is picked up again on every cron run. Increment `retryCount` in that case too, so the cleanup eventually removes it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The comment above the deleteMany no longer matches the query, which now also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1 of any method.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says the query deletes only SMS reminders whose scheduled date has passed. After this change, the OR also deletes every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, whatever its date or method. Someone reading the comment will expect only past SMS reminders to be removed, not future ones that failed repeatedly or email/WhatsApp ones. Update the comment to describe the retry branch. If deleting non-SMS reminders is not intended, add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch so the code matches the comment.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new backup-code branch is checked before the TOTP branch and ignores `credentials.totpCode`. The existing password check (line 121, `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`) is skipped whenever totpCode is non-empty. WHY: A request with `totpCode=anything` and a valid `backupCode` skips both the password check and TOTP validation. Anyone holding one leaked backup code can log in as the user without the password; the same applies to the SSO checks at lines 113/117. HOW: Check the password regardless of totpCode when a backupCode is supplied, or reject requests that carry both totpCode and backupCode before branching.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The one-time backup code is consumed with a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write. `user.backupCodes` is read at the top of authorize(), and later an unconditional `prisma.user.update` writes the re-encrypted array. WHY: Two concurrent logins with the same code both pass the indexOf check, so the 'single-use' code is used twice. Two concurrent logins with different codes each write back their own stale array, which brings back the code the other request consumed. HOW: Do the update inside a transaction with a row lock, or make it conditional on the old value (`where: { id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }`) and fail the login when no row is updated.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString('hex')` in setup.ts:61), but matching uses an exact `indexOf` without normalizing case. The input placeholder is 'XXXXX-XXXXX' (BackupCode.tsx:21). WHY: A user who types a code in uppercase, as the placeholder suggests, gets IncorrectBackupCode and is locked out of the recovery flow. disable.ts:61 has the same problem. HOW: Use `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '').toLowerCase()` (and the same normalization in disable.ts).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: On the new DisplayBackupCodes step, 2FA is already enabled on the server (handleEnable now calls setStep instead of onEnable). onEnable and resetState only run from the 'Close' button. Dismissing the Dialog with Escape or an outside click goes through the parent's `onOpenChange` (two-factor-auth.tsx:64), which only toggles `open`. WHY: The parent's onEnable side effects (switch state/refetch) are skipped, so the UI shows 2FA as disabled while it is enabled. The modal also keeps step=DisplayBackupCodes, password, and codes in state, so reopening it shows the old backup-code screen. HOW: Handle dismissal in onOpenChange: when the step is DisplayBackupCodes, call resetState() and onEnable().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `req.body.backupCode` is used without a type check and then `.replaceAll` is called on it. WHY: A truthy non-string body value (number, array, object) throws a TypeError, which surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. HOW: Validate with `typeof req.body.backupCode === 'string'` (or a zod schema) before use.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Backup codes are checked against the user's input with indexOf, which is not a constant-time comparison.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The backup code is a second-factor secret, but it is checked with `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` (here and in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61). That comparison exits early, so its timing can leak information about the stored codes. Instead, compare the input against every stored code with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length Buffers. Skip null entries, check all codes without returning early, and lowercase the input so it matches the hex format.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Using a backup code is a non-atomic read-then-write, so concurrent logins can reuse one code or bring back a code that was already used.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Using a backup code is not atomic. `user.backupCodes` is read at the start of `authorize`, decrypted, the matched slot is set to null in memory, and the whole array is written back with an unconditional `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent logins with the same code both find it in the stale copy and both succeed, so the code works more than once. Two concurrent logins with different codes overwrite each other, and the last write puts the other used code back so it can be used again. Do the read and the write inside a transaction with a row lock (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`). Or make the write conditional: `updateMany({ where: { id: user.id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }, data: {...} })`, and reject the login if `count === 0`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: This assertion is always truthy, so it can't catch the new backup-codes step that keeps 2FA from showing as enabled.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` checks a Promise, which is always truthy, so it can never fail. With this PR, a valid OTP now shows the backup-codes step, and `onEnable` (which flips the switch) only runs after `backup-codes-close` is clicked. This test never clicks it, so the switch is likely still unchecked here, yet the test passes. Click `backup-codes-close` first, then assert `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]')).toBeVisible()` as the second test does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The download and copy checks only look at the filename and the toast, so they would pass with empty or wrong backup codes.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The copy test only waits for `toast-success`. EnableTwoFactorModal shows that toast right after calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, without awaiting it or checking what was copied, so the test passes even if the copied text is wrong or empty. The download test only checks the filename. Read the downloaded file (or the clipboard, with permissions granted) and check that it holds 10 codes in XXXXX-XXXXX format that match the codes stored in the DB.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `disable()` gained a required `backupCode` parameter, but `components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38` still calls it with two arguments.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `disable` now takes a required third argument, `backupCode: string`. Only the settings modal was updated. `apps/web/components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38` still calls `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode)`. If that file imports this module, the call fails type-checking (expected 3 arguments, got 2). Either make the parameter optional or update that caller too.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: BackupCode component's default export is named TwoFactor.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This file renders the backup-code input, but its default export is still named `TwoFactor`, copied from TwoFactor.tsx. DisableTwoFactorModal and login.tsx import both components, so React DevTools, stack traces and anyone reading the code will see two components called TwoFactor. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Log message in the disable-2FA endpoint says 'backup code login'.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This error log was copied from next-auth-options.ts. It says the server cannot continue with a backup code *login*, but this endpoint disables 2FA. Whoever reads the logs will look in the login flow instead of this route. Change the wording to describe disabling 2FA.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The constructor parameter changed from the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Code like `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId`, or `teamId: undefined`, now type-checks. WHY: The compiler no longer catches this. At runtime `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse` rejects it, `this.options` becomes null, and every query quietly uses `1=0`, so team insights come back empty instead of failing loudly. HOW: Keep `options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (the z.infer discriminated union) in the constructor signature, or make `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` a discriminated union that requires `teamId` when `scope` is "team".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: In getBaseConditions, the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches can never run, because authConditions is always a non-null Prisma.Sql.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `authConditions` can never be null or falsy: every path in `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns a `Prisma.Sql`, including `NOTHING_CONDITION`. The `else if (filterConditions)` and `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION }` branches are therefore dead code. They suggest a 'filters only' path that does not exist. If someone later changes the auth builder to return null for 'unrestricted', that branch would silently drop authorization. Simplify so the code says what it actually does: the auth condition always applies, and filters are added with AND when present.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` fails in two ways. First, String#scrub only exists in Ruby 2.1+, and the project's CI (.travis.yml) runs Ruby 2.0.0. Second, SimpleRSS returns nil for `content` on standard RSS 2.0 items that only have <description>. Either case raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole import: the job has retry: false and no rescue. TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute synchronously, so the same error also stops the fetch_http fallback from running. Fix: use `(i.content || i.description).to_s`, and only call scrub if it is available (or use encode with invalid: :replace).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: `url` is interpolated unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>`. The remote page content from Readability (which allows `href`, so `javascript:` links survive) and the RSS content are also stored as raw HTML with cook_method raw_html. embed_url comes from an unauthenticated request parameter: EmbedController only checks the spoofable Referer and that the host matches embeddable_host. An attacker can therefore request a URL such as `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` or point at attacker-influenced pages on that host. The resulting post is rendered without sanitization in both the forum topic view and the embed view, giving stored XSS on the Discourse origin. Fix: escape `url` (ERB::Util.html_escape / CGI.escapeHTML), and run the imported HTML through a sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist that rejects non-http(s) hrefs) before storing it.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: `cook` now returns `raw` verbatim for raw_html posts and skips the whole cooking and sanitization pipeline. The cook method persists on the post, so every later revision through PostRevisor is also stored as unsanitized HTML, including edits by anyone who can edit the post (owner, staff). Whatever HTML ends up in raw (remote page content, RSS content, edits) is served as-is in the forum, which creates a persistent XSS sink. Sanitize the HTML here, for example with the same whitelist approach PrettyText uses, instead of returning raw unchanged.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: The throttle is keyed on the full embed_url, so an anonymous client can bypass it by changing the path or query string. Each request enqueues a RetrieveTopic job (EmbedController#best only checks a spoofable Referer). Each job synchronously re-runs Jobs::PollFeed: it downloads the entire feed and calls TopicEmbed.import for every item. It then makes a remote fetch via `open(url)` with no timeout. One unauthenticated client can flood Sidekiq with feed polls and blocking HTTP requests. Fix: throttle globally or per IP rather than per URL, don't call PollFeed inline (rely on the hourly job or a single global lock), and set open-uri read/open timeouts.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `post = embed.post` is used without a nil check. If the embedded post was hard-deleted, PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises. Every feed poll that contains this URL then crashes, and that also aborts the remaining feed items. Guard the nil case (recreate the post or skip it).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The postMessage origin check is a substring test, so a lookalike origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl is accepted.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The origin check is a substring test (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)`), not an exact match. Any origin that is a prefix of the Discourse URL passes. For example, an attacker who registers `forum.example.co` can send messages that the embedding page accepts for `forum.example.com`. Today the message only resizes the iframe, but this is a weak trust check for any future message type. Parse the Discourse origin once and compare it exactly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The post date uses a fixed English strftime format instead of I18n localisation.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `post.created_at.strftime("%e %b %Y")` always shows English month abbreviations, whatever the site locale is. Every other string in this view goes through I18n.t, so on a non-English forum the date is the only untranslated text in the embed. Use `I18n.l(post.created_at.to_date, format: ...)` or a locale-defined date format instead.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The URL in the 'imported from' link is put into HTML without escaping, and that HTML is later rendered raw.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The embed URL comes from the RSS item link or id, or from the embed_url request parameter. It is placed into `#{url}` with no escaping. The post is created with cook_method raw_html, so `cook` returns raw unchanged, and best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked`. A URL containing `'` or `<` can break out of the attribute or inject markup into the text shown to users. Escape it with `ERB::Util.html_escape(url)` before interpolating.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Protocol-relative URLs ('//cdn.host/x') are treated as host-relative and rewritten to 'http://host/cdn.host/x'.
suggestions.suggestionContent: absolutize_urls treats any href/src that starts with '/' as host-relative, which includes protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/img.png'. The regex removes all leading slashes and adds the embed host, giving 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png', so imported images and links from CDNs break. Handle the '//' prefix first by prepending only the scheme, then handle single-slash paths.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The origin check accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl instead of requiring an exact origin match.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The postMessage origin check uses a substring test (and not even an anchored prefix test). A shorter or truncated origin, such as the same host with a missing last character, is accepted. Compare the received origin exactly against the origin parsed from discourseUrl.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: For `raw_html` posts, `Post#cook` now returns `self.raw` and ignores the text passed to it. Callers that cook text other than the post's current raw get the wrong result. For example, `lib/tasks/add_topic_to_quotes.rake:5` calls `p.cook(new_raw, ...)` and would get the old raw back, so the new content is dropped. Return the first argument instead: `return args.first if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`.

suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The port check ignores the scheme, so non-default ports 80 or 443 are dropped from absolutized URLs.

suggestions.suggestionContent: In SimpleRSS, `i.content` is only set for Atom <content> elements. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `import` checks for an existing embed and then creates a topic, post and TopicEmbed, with no lock. Two runs can overlap: RetrieveTopic jobs for different URLs both call PollFeed#execute, and the hourly PollFeed job runs too. Both can see `embed.blank?` for the same URL. The second `TopicEmbed.create!` then hits the unique index on embed_url and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which makes the job fail. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: If the embedded post has been destroyed, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError on every later feed poll for that URL. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `execute(...)[0]['id']` (and the same for `uncategorized_category_id` at line 15) assumes the query returns a row. If `embed_category` was never set, or its value doesn't match a category name, the result is empty. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: hosts from the old setting are split on "\n" and inserted as-is through string interpolation. A value containing a quote breaks the INSERT and aborts the migration. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the column, not `uri.host`. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: every key matching `*_ids` is now mapped through `_lookupSubType` and the original key is always deleted. Ids that can't be resolved become `undefined` entries, and a null `*_ids` value throws on `.map`. WHY: existing REST models with `*_ids` fields lose that data (replaced by arrays of undefined) or crash during hydration when no matching sideloaded collection exists. `hydrated || []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array. HOW: guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])`, only replace/delete when the sideloaded collection exists, and filter out unresolved ids.

suggestions.suggestionContent: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the INNER JOIN returns a row. suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The query lowercases the stored host but not the incoming URI host, so referers with mixed-case hostnames are rejected.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the stored column. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test passes only because has_topic_embed? is false on an unsaved topic; it does not test the absence of embeddable hosts.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The host lookup lowercases only the stored host, not the incoming referer host, so a referer with uppercase letters never matches its allowed host.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Only the stored side of the comparison is normalised: `lower(host)` is compared against `uri.host` with its original case. Domains are case-insensitive, so an allowed host gets rejected when the Referer or embed URL has uppercase letters, and TopicEmbed then picks no category. Lowercase both sides, and ideally also lowercase the host when it is saved.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `_hydrateEmbedded` now deletes every `*_ids` key and replaces it with possibly-undefined lookups, which breaks existing consumers that read the raw ids.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Before this change, the regex `/(.+)\_id$/` did not match keys ending in `_ids`, so models kept fields like `group_ids` / `category_ids` exactly as the server sent them. Now any key ending in `_ids` gets `delete obj[k]` unconditionally. Its value moves to `obj[pluralize(subType)]` as the result of `_lookupSubType` for each id, which is `undefined` when the response doesn't sideload that type. Any existing REST-store model or template that reads a raw `*_ids` array loses it. The pluralized property can also overwrite a real field of the same name. To fix: only replace and delete the key when every id resolves (the singular branch already does this with its `if (hydrated)` check), and otherwise leave `obj[k]` as it was.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The migration copies old setting values unchanged, including scheme and path, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares stored values with a bare uri.host, so migrated URL-style entries never match.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting accepted full URLs such as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`; the old specs used exactly these values. This migration inserts each line as it is, with raw SQL, so the model's `before_validation` normalization never runs. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-17) looks up rows with `lower(host) = uri.host`, which assumes stored values are bare, normalized hostnames. Migrated rows that still have a scheme or path will never match. EmbedController will reject those referers and TopicRetriever will treat them as invalid, so embedding breaks on upgraded sites. Normalize each value before inserting: strip whitespace, `sub(/^https?:\/\//,'')`, `sub(/\/.*$/,'')`, and skip blank lines. Escape the value too (for example with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration crashes when the `embed_category` row is missing from site_settings, which is the case whenever the setting was left at its default. `execute(...)[0]` is nil, so `['id']` raises NoMethodError. The uncategorized_category_id lookup has the same problem. Hosts are also inserted as raw strings. Values with an http(s):// prefix or a path, which the old setting allowed, are stored as-is and will never match `uri.host` in `record_for_host`, so embedding breaks after the upgrade. A single quote in a value also breaks the INSERT. Fix: check the row count before indexing, strip the scheme and path from each host, and quote values with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!` without checking for nil. Saving through the admin controller without a host param, or validating `EmbeddableHost.new`, raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard it with `if self.host.present?` (or use safe navigation) and add `validates :host, presence: true`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The plural branch runs on every key ending in `_ids`. It calls `obj[k].map` without a null check, so a null value throws. It also always deletes the original id array, even when `_lookupSubType` finds no matching collection in the root and returns undefined for every id. Any rest-serialized payload with a plain id array (e.g. `user_ids`) therefore loses its ids and gets an array of undefined instead. Only replace and delete the key when `obj[k]` is an array and the plural collection exists in the root.

suggestions.label: bug

An unknown or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find` (raises RecordNotFound, which is handled) or add an explicit nil check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` redefines and replaces `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, because Ruby has no method overloading. WHY: app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments, so it now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, given 5, expected 3..4) and emoji resizing breaks. HOW: give the new method a different name (e.g. `downsize_to(from, to, dimensions, opts)`), or keep one method that tells the two forms apart by argument count, and update the uploads controller to match.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `tempfile.path` is passed to OptimizedImage.downsize, which interpolates it unescaped into a backtick shell command (`convert_with`, optimized_image.rb:161). For API URL uploads, that path is built by `FileHelper.download` as `Tempfile.new(["discourse-upload-#{type}", extension])`, where `type` is `params.require(:type)` and `extension` comes from the URL. WHY: an API caller can put shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, `$( )`, backticks) in `type` or the URL extension and run arbitrary commands on the server. Before this change, this tempfile path never reached a shell. HOW: whitelist `type`, and escape every argument with Shellwords.escape, or run the command with an array form (Open3/system with separate args) instead of backticks.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the animated branch in `optimize` is chosen only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here `from` is the Rack multipart tempfile path, which has no original extension, so animated GIFs always go through `downsize_instructions`, which reads `#{from}[0]`. WHY: an oversized animated GIF is silently flattened to its first frame, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. HOW: decide whether the file is animated from `filename` (the original name) or the detected file type, not from the tempfile path.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: each loop iteration spawns ImageMagick and then runs ImageOptim on images up to 10MB, and the loop does not stop when `downsize` returns false or the size stays the same. WHY: a failed or ineffective conversion still uses all 5 expensive passes. For synchronous API uploads this blocks the request thread for a long time, which allows CPU exhaustion through repeated large uploads. HOW: stop the loop when `downsize` returns false or the size does not decrease, and skip ImageOptim on intermediate passes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the client-side limit is now a hard-coded 10MB for every upload `type`, replacing `max_<type>_size_kb`, so attachments are no longer checked against `max_attachment_size_kb`. WHY: users can pick attachments larger than the configured limit, upload them in full, and only then get a server-side rejection. The error messages here and in the 413 handler also show 10MB instead of the real limit. HOW: keep the 10MB limit only for images (`type === 'image'`) and use `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for other types.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The file_too_large message now always says the limit is 10240 KB, even for attachments, where the server enforces max_attachment_size_kb.
suggestions.suggestionContent: maxSizeKB is now hard-coded to 10 MB for every upload type. Only images are downsized on the server (uploads_controller.rb:63-70). Attachments are still limited by SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb (upload.rb:169). As a result, attachments up to 10 MB get past this check, and the translated `post.errors.file_too_large` message shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the limit actually enforced. Use 10 MB only when type is 'image', and keep Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] for the other types so the message shows the real limit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The second `downsize` definition replaces the 5-argument version, so existing callers like resize_emoji.rb now raise ArgumentError.

The existing caller `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 now raises ArgumentError (5 arguments given, 3..4 expected), which breaks emoji resizing. Fix it in one of two ways: keep a single method that accepts both forms (e.g. `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height = nil, opts = {})` and build the dimensions only when a height is given), or update every caller to pass a single dimensions string such as "100x100".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new 4-arg `downsize`, added for the upload controller's "80%" call, silently replaces the existing width/height `downsize`.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby has no method overloading, so the second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined just above it. The new controller call (`downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`) works only because of this replacement. Any existing caller that passes max_width and max_height now breaks: with 5 args it raises ArgumentError, and with 4 args `max_height` is read as `opts`, giving the wrong geometry. Fix: drop the width/height variant and update its callers, or give the percentage variant its own name (e.g. `downsize_by(from, to, dimensions, opts)`) and call that from the controller.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The second `self.downsize` definition replaces the 5-argument one, so the existing 5-argument caller now gets an ArgumentError.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` definition at line 145, so that earlier version is dead code. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` (resize_emoji.rb:14) still passes 5 arguments and will now raise ArgumentError. Fix: merge the two into one method that accepts both forms, for example `def self.downsize(from, to, dim_or_w, h_or_opts=nil, opts={})`, or give the dimension-string version a different name, or update the caller to pass `"100x100"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The client-side check now uses a hardcoded 10MB for every upload type and ignores the per-type limit settings.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` but under 10MB now pass the client check and are then rejected by the server. Images above the limit now pass on purpose, because the server downsizes them. Keep the per-type setting for non-image types and apply the 10MB ceiling only to images.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: A second `self.downsize` definition replaces the 5-argument version, so ResizeEmoji's `downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` raises ArgumentError.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The client upload size check is now hardcoded to 10MB for every type, so it ignores the attachment size setting.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Only images are downsized on the server, so only images should get the fixed 10MB client cap. As written, the check is wrong for attachments in both directions. If `max_attachment_size_kb` is above 10MB, valid attachments are rejected before upload. If it is below 10MB, oversized attachments pass the client check, upload fully, and then fail on the server. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through removes the group_users rows with delete_all, so no callbacks run. GroupUser's `counter_cache: "user_count"` never decrements, and the primary_group_id cleanup from the old `destroy_deletions` path is skipped. The removed user can also keep the group as their primary_group_id (title/flair). HOW: Use `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all` (as `Group#remove` already does), then `User.where(id: user_id, primary_group_id: group.id).update_all(primary_group_id: nil)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: add_members calls `group.add(user)` (`users.push`) for every username without checking whether the user is already a member. WHY: group_users has a UNIQUE (group_id, user_id) index, so adding someone who is already in the group raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and returns a 500. Any users in the same request that were not yet added are dropped. The old `usernames=` setter avoided this by diffing against the current members. HOW: Skip existing members, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.exists?(user.id)`.

WHY: With 50 members and limit 50 the UI shows '1/2' and enables 'next', which loads an empty page. On that empty page currentPage equals totalPages, so the paging state shown is wrong.
